root_cause: The first lifecycle implementation treated company context primarily as one stage at a time. Entrepreneurs can be in a primary company phase while simultaneously raising funding, buying a company, preparing succession, automating growth, improving valuation or integrating an acquisition. Portal and Brain therefore needed a composable context model rather than a single-stage switch.
prevention_rule: Every material Portal/Brain recommendation must be able to consume one evidence-backed primary company phase plus zero or more strategic-event overlays, entrepreneur goals, business-health dimensions, capability maturity and historical context records. Package tier must remain orthogonal: it controls operating envelope, not business meaning. Unproven phases must remain visibly unproven.

evidence.outcome: Portal and Powerhouse now share a composable business context with primary phase, concurrent events/goals, health, maturity, history, journey, relevant models/pages and context-aware decision/executive projections.
